newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end firmer, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end firmer, seen consolidating.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed slightly firmer on Tuesday and dealers expected the rates to consolidate around current levels amid stable liquidity situation in the banking system.
The overnight interbank rate closed at 5.075 percent against Monday's 4.996 close, with 30-day commercial paper stabilising at 5.05 percent.

Tuesday's payment deadline s for the Finance Ministry's T$35 billion auction of seven-year bonds tightened liquidity slightly but dealers said they did not expect a further squeeze as routine payrolls soon would return to the banking system.
The bond market was quiet on a lack of market-moving factors, traders said.
Also quieting sentiment was caution ahead of the Finance Ministry's December 17 auction of T$50 billion in government bonds -- the biggest such cash call in five years.
The bonds, to be issued on December 20, would have a 10-year term and coupon rate of 6.80 percent, ministry officials said.
